events.ai_basis: A first version of the proof of the main theorem was obtained through interactive sessions with ChatGPT 5.6 and Gemini 3.1. In addition, the counterexamples were constructed entirely by these AI systems.

why: The statement names the Guralnick–Thompson conjecture on composition factors of genus-0 groups, i.e. finiteness of the non-alternating, non-abelian simple composition factors. Frohardt–Magaard (Annals 2001) state in their abstract that they prove that conjecture, in the general genus-g form that includes genus 0; an Annals acceptance is a journal of record, so it is whole/digested and pre-snapshot. Shih 1991 is a pre-snapshot case (linear type-A family), digested via the approved thesis. Every post-snapshot event is about something else: Neftin–Zieve and Gerhardt–McKemmie–Neftin classify full monodromy groups (large degree, product type, type B), which is a different question from composition-factor finiteness, and their own introduction says the composition-factor consequence was already known, so I scored them variant rather than case; Behajaina–König–Neftin is polynomial monodromy; Liao–Wang–Zhang and Sheinfeld concern the unrelated class-squares Thompson conjecture (F15). Sheinfeld's acknowledgement credits AI with the first proof and the counterexamples, so that event's ai_role is generated, but it is a different problem and is discarded as variant. Liao–Wang–Zhang has none_found false with empty systems, so none.
doubts: The Frohardt–Magaard theorem statement was not read; whole rests on the abstract's claim that it proves the 1990 conjecture plus snippets that genus 0 is covered. If the bullet means the explicit list of genus-0 groups, or if Aschbacher's 'genus-0 systems' form a wider class than monodromy groups, it would be a case and the list remains open; the record's competing_reading raises this, but the bullet's wording names a conjecture, which is the finiteness claim. Gerhardt–McKemmie–Neftin could be read as a case of the explicit-list reading; I rejected that reading.
